target.title: fix(video-generation): DashScope downloads hang when CDN body stalls after headers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two related issues where DashScope-compatible generated-video downloads (Alibaba Wan / Qwen) could:

1. **Hang forever** when the CDN returns HTTP 200 headers but never sends body chunks. `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` clears its abort once headers arrive, so a stalled body had no timeout at all on `main`.

2. **Silently fall back to the 120s default** when a function-valued remaining deadline was exhausted (returned 0). The resolver gate `resolved > 0` dropped the exhausted budget, and `readResponseWithLimit` skips chunk idle timeout when `chunkTimeoutMs` is 0/falsy, so a zero budget would read the body unbounded instead of failing fast.

Affected workflow: `runDashscopeVideoGenerationTask` → `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` → `readResponseWithLimit`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Extracted `resolveDashscopeVideoDownloadTimeoutMs`**: single resolver for both the fetch GET timeout and the post-header body chunk-idle timeout, replacing the inline ternary at the fetch call site.

- **Changed resolver gate from `resolved > 0` to `Math.max(0, Math.floor(resolved))`**: preserves zero/negative values from function-valued remaining budgets so the header fetch and body stage see the same exhausted deadline. Falls back to `defaultTimeoutMs ?? 120_000` only for truly undefined/missing timeouts.

- **Added `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` to `readResponseWithLimit`**: the body read now carries the same resolved download timeout as the GET request. A stalled CDN body fails closed with `"…download stalled: no data received for Nms"` instead of hanging.

- **Added body-stage exhausted-budget check (`downloadTimeoutMs <= 0`)**: when the function-valued timeout returns 0 after headers (full budget consumed by GET), throws `"…remaining budget exhausted"` immediately — matching the error contract `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` callers already expect for timeout failures.

Non-goals: BytePlus/OpenAI/Fal/Runway extension-local download paths; music `provider-assets`; changing shared `readResponseWithLimit` defaults.

**Collision check:** searched open PRs for `dashscope-compatible.ts` and `resolveDashscopeVideoDownloadTimeoutMs`; no same-file or same-problem open PR found. Related #108982 bounds other vendor download sites but does not touch this shared DashScope helper.

## User Impact

| Scenario | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| CDN body stalls after headers | Infinite hang until process exit | Fails closed: `"…download stalled: no data received for Nms"` |
| Complete body within budget | Works | Still works (unchanged) |
| Function-valued timeout exhausted | Falls back to 120s default, then hangs on 0 chunkTimeoutMs | Fails closed: `"…remaining budget exhausted"` in <5ms |

## Verification

- Exact head: `456184f3a3c2d06560908cbe63f3220ec1bc183d`
- `oxfmt --check src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts` — passed.
- `oxlint` on changed files — clean (pre-existing failure in `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` is unrelated, also present on `main`).
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos > aborts a stalled generated video body via chunk idle timeout 301ms
 ✓ downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos > persists a complete generated video body before the idle deadline 6ms
 ✓ downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos > fails closed when a function-valued remaining budget is exhausted 3ms
 ✓ downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos loopback HTTP > bounds a stalled loopback HTTP body with a real server 224ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

- Sibling lane (unchanged callers still green):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qwen/video-generation-provider.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- **Mutation check — exhausted budget P1**: temporarily revert `resolved > 0` → `Math.max(0, Math.floor(resolved))` and remove the body-stage `downloadTimeoutMs <= 0` throw → test 3 hangs indefinitely → restore → test 3 passes in 3ms.
- **Mutation check — chunk idle timeout**: temporarily remove `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` from `readResponseWithLimit` call → test 1 hangs indefinitely → restore → test 1 passes in 301ms.

## Real behavior proof

### 1. Chunk idle timeout (positive control)

Stalled `ReadableStream` body with `timeoutMs: 80` rejects in 301ms with `"Alibaba Wan generated video download stalled: no data received for 80ms"` — bounded, not an indefinite hang.

### 2. Complete body (valid response)

Complete body (`mp4-bytes`) still succeeds under `timeoutMs: 5000` in 6ms — normal path unaffected.

### 3. Exhausted budget (negative → positive control)

`timeoutMs: () => 0` (function-valued, header fetch consumed entire budget) rejects in 3ms with `"…remaining budget exhausted"` — fails closed instead of falling back to the 120s default + unbounded body read.

### 4. Loopback HTTP (real TCP stall)

Real `http.createServer` at 127.0.0.1 writes `"first-chunk"` then stalls (simulates stalled CDN). `timeoutMs: 200`, uses real `fetch`. Rejects in 224ms — proves the chunk-idle timeout catches a real TCP stall in production code, not just a mock `ReadableStream`.

### Not tested

Live DashScope CDN stalls against `dashscope.aliyuncs.com` — requires real API credentials.

## Risk / Compatibility

Adds fail-closed body idle where `main` previously had none (infinite hang). Uses existing operation timeout budget — no new config/env. AI-assisted.
